newsitem.title: ALBANIA: IMF says ready to help Albania over savings crisis.
newsitem.headline: IMF says ready to help Albania over savings crisis.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Tuesday it was ready to do "everything" that it could to help the Albanian government overcome a financial crisis sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes.

The IMF's resident representative in Albania, John King, told Reuters the Washington-based group was already providing technical assistance over the failure of the hugely popular savings schemes and had offered any further help needed.

"The IMF will do everything it can to assist the government in resolving the crisis," King said. The IMF has already provided two lending facilities to Albania since 1992 and is currently negotiating a third loan programme.
King declined to say what sort of financial facilities the IMF might offer Albania's right-wing government to settle the current crisis, which has unleashed a wave of violent nationwide protests.
Economists believe Albanians might have plunged more than $1.0 billion into the high-yielding pyramid schemes that mushroomed across the country after the old communist regime fell in 1990.

Five of the top nine national schemes have either declared bankruptcy or have had their bank assets seized by the government. The other four are still making interest payments but are not allowing investors to withdraw their capital.
